subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw apply when an active session transcript is too large or repeatedly crashes the gateway during reload?
rationale: The code-level problem is real, but choosing between quarantine, truncation, skip/reset, media dedupe, and doctor-assisted recovery affects persistent user transcript data and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Default Quarantine With Doctor Recovery
options.body: Mark the session degraded before whole-file repair/open, skip it for automatic restart recovery, and provide `openclaw doctor --fix` or an equivalent visible recovery path to archive, trim, or reset it.

options.title: Bounded Automatic Truncation
options.body: Automatically retain the newest safe transcript window and compact/archive older content, accepting a stronger data-retention tradeoff for hands-free recovery.

options.title: Bootstrap-Only Mitigation First
options.body: Land only the bootstrap-marker cap now and leave transcript-size and media recovery to later, accepting that the main crash loop can still recur on oversized files.

recommendation.title: Default Quarantine With Doctor Recovery
recommendation.body: Mark the session degraded before whole-file repair/open, skip it for automatic restart recovery, and provide `openclaw doctor --fix` or an equivalent visible recovery path to archive, trim, or reset it.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history owner across the active runner, bootstrap scan, session-manager, and repair surfaces.
